title: Nicknames like King and Kid, and playing in funerals as the clarinet wizard
summary: Few clarinetists took titles; he recalls a parade with two clarinets in different keys.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, there aren't many clarinet players called Kit, are they? That's mostly trumpet players. No, no clarinet players. No.

The only one that called himself Kit was Wayne Smolga. Yeah. At least he had a sense of humor. Well, like, Kid Ari is a trauma-in-law, doesn't it? Kid Avery, Joe Avery. And Kid Williams, A. Well, anyway. But I never can recall a clarinet play doing that except for the moment of all. Kid Ernest. Well, I've heard people call you the clarinet wizard. You know? Yeah. I'd hear them say that in the street. I remember one time you played a parade with Joe H. Lewis, you know, and the crowd was talking about, you know. He was playing E-flat and you were playing B-flat. Yeah. Remember, like, near the Tulane Club? It was a funeral, I can't remember. I think that dude, yeah. It was a funeral, wasn't it? I believe. I believe. Anyway. That was unusual to have the two clarinets like that. Yeah. You don't hear that anymore. No. Was he ever playing bands with two clarinets?
